sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>
sections.docs:
<docs>
Pi documentation (read only when the user asks about pi itself, its SDK, extensions, themes, skills, or TUI):
- Main documentation: <vol>/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/README.md
- Additional docs: <vol>/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs
- Examples: <vol>/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples (extensions, custom tools, SDK)
- When reading pi docs or examples, resolve docs/... under Additional docs and examples/... under Examples, not the current working directory
- When asked about: extensions (docs/extensions.md, examples/extensions/), themes (docs/themes.md), skills (docs/skills.md), prompt templates (docs/prompt-templates.md), TUI components (docs/tui.md), keybindings (docs/keybindings.md), SDK integrations (docs/sdk.md), custom providers (docs/custom-provider.md), adding models (docs/models.md), pi packages (docs/packages.md), environment variables (docs/environment-variables.md), MCP servers (docs/mcp.md), codemode scripts and non-LLM models such as classifiers and image models (docs/codemode.md)
- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing
- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)
</docs>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Ceate an SVG of an awkward family portrait of robots. Give each robot a distinct personality, and suggest their relationships through poses and composition. No text.

Deliver the result as image and/or video files, working in the current directory.
- Save the finished files in ./output/. Only what is in ./output/ is published as the result, so
  ./output/ holds those finished image/video files and nothing else.
- Formats: images as .png, .jpg, .webp, .gif or .svg; videos as .mp4 or .webm. At most 8 files,
  each under 2 MB; videos at most 10 seconds.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.15.0 (standard library only), node 26.11.1 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 9.0.2, ffprobe 9.0.2. Don't install packages or download anything.
- Keep the code you write to make the files in the working directory (its root, or a subdirectory
  like ./src/, but not in ./output/): it's published as the source. Delete intermediate files such
  as rendered frames when you're done.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pure-python PNG reader that prints an ASCII-art view of an image.

Usage: pngview.py FILE [COLS] [ROWS] [--hue]
"""
import sys
import zlib
import struct


def read_png(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a PNG'
    pos = 8
    idat = b''
    meta = {}
    while pos < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[pos:pos + 4])[0]
        typ = data[pos + 4:pos + 8]
        chunk = data[pos + 8:pos + 8 + ln]
        pos += 12 + ln
        if typ == b'IHDR':
            w, h, bd, ct, cm, fm, il = struct.unpack('>IIBBBBB', chunk)
            meta = dict(w=w, h=h, bd=bd, ct=ct)
        elif typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += chunk
        elif typ == b'IEND':
            break
    w, h, bd, ct = meta['w'], meta['h'], meta['bd'], meta['ct']
    assert bd == 8 and ct in (0, 2, 4, 6), f'unsupported png bd={bd} ct={ct}'
    nch = {0: 1, 2: 3, 4: 2, 6: 4}[ct]
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    stride = w * nch
    out = bytearray(h * stride)
    prev = bytearray(stride)
    p = 0
    for y in range(h):
        f = raw[p]
        p += 1
        line = bytearray(raw[p:p + stride])
        p += stride
        if f == 1:
            for i in range(nch, stride):
                line[i] = (line[i] + line[i - nch]) & 255
        elif f == 2:
            for i in range(stride):
                line[i] = (line[i] + prev[i]) & 255
        elif f == 3:
            for i in range(stride):
                a = line[i - nch] if i >= nch else 0
                line[i] = (line[i] + ((a + prev[i]) >> 1)) & 255
        elif f == 4:
            for i in range(stride):
                a = line[i - nch] if i >= nch else 0
                b = prev[i]
                c = prev[i - nch] if i >= nch else 0
                pa, pb, pc = abs(b - c), abs(a - c), abs(a + b - 2 * c)
                if pa <= pb and pa <= pc:
                    pr = a
                elif pb <= pc:
                    pr = b
                else:
                    pr = c
                line[i] = (line[i] + pr) & 255
        out[y * stride:(y + 1) * stride] = line
        prev = line
    return w, h, nch, out


def sample(x, y):
    """mean color of cell at pixel coords (x0,y0)-(x1,y1)"""
    pass


def view(path, cols=100, rows=None, hue=False, box=None):
    w, h, nch, buf = read_png(path)
    if rows is None:
        rows = max(1, int(cols * h / w / 2))
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = box if box else (0, 0, w, h)
    bw = (x1 - x0) / cols
    bh = (y1 - y0) / rows
    ramp = ' .:-=+*#%@'
    lines = []
    for ry in range(rows):
        sy0 = y0 + ry * bh
        sy1 = min(y0 + (ry + 1) * bh, y1)
        row = []
        for rx in range(cols):
            sx0 = x0 + rx * bw
            sx1 = min(x0 + (rx + 1) * bw, x1)
            rs = gs = bs = n = 0
            # sample a few pixels inside the cell (subsample if big)
            stepx = max(1, int(bw / 4))
            stepy = max(1, int(bh / 4))
            for yy in range(int(sy0), int(sy1), stepy):
                for xx in range(int(sx0), int(sx1), stepx):
                    i = (yy * w + xx) * nch
                    if nch == 1:
                        r = g = b = buf[i]
                    else:
                        r, g, b = buf[i], buf[i + 1], buf[i + 2]
                    rs += r; gs += g; bs += b; n += 1
            if n == 0:
                row.append(' ')
                continue
            r, g, b = rs / n, gs / n, bs / n
            lum = 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b
            if hue:
                mx, mn = max(r, g, b), min(r, g, b)
                sat = 0 if mx == 0 else (mx - mn) / mx
                if sat < 0.25:
                    row.append(ramp[min(9, int(lum / 256 * 10))])
                else:
                    if r >= g >= b or r >= b >= g:
                        c = 'R' if r > 140 else 'r'
                    elif g >= r >= b or g >= b >= r:
                        c = 'G' if g > 140 else 'g'
                    else:
                        c = 'B' if b > 140 else 'b'
                    row.append(c if lum > 60 else c.lower())
            else:
                row.append(ramp[min(9, int(lum / 256 * 10))])
        lines.append(''.join(row))
    return lines


if __name__ == '__main__':
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith('--')]
    flags = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a.startswith('--')]
    path = args[0]
    cols = int(args[1]) if len(args) > 1 else 100
    rows = int(args[2]) if len(args) > 2 else None
    hue = '--hue' in flags
    box = None
    if '--box' in flags:
        i = sys.argv.index('--box') + 1
        box = tuple(int(v) for v in sys.argv[i:i + 4])
    print(f'== {path} ==')
    for ln in view(path, cols, rows, hue, box):
        print(ln)

import sys
sys.path.insert(0,'src')
from pngview import read_png

PAL = [
 ('G',(0xa8,0x76,0x48)),  # grandpa arm/rust
 ('g',(0xc0,0x90,0x64)),  # grandpa torso light
 ('p',(0x5c,0x46,0x32)),  # grandpa shoes
 ('M',(0xf7,0xef,0xdf)),  # mom cream
 ('R',(0xdc,0x98,0xa4)),  # mom rose
 ('r',(0xb8,0x5c,0x68)),  # mom accent
 ('D',(0x8d,0xab,0xc9)),  # dad blue light
 ('d',(0x55,0x76,0x99)),  # dad blue arm
 ('T',(0xd9,0x55,0x40)),  # tie red
 ('N',(0x4d,0x54,0x5f)),  # teen graphite
 ('E',(0x7d,0xff,0x8a)),  # neon
 ('A',(0x57,0xc4,0xb4)),  # daughter teal
 ('S',(0xf7,0xd6,0x78)),  # son yellow
 ('O',(0xc0,0x8a,0x5b)),  # dog copper
 ('P',(0x40,0x60,0x3f)),  # plant
 ('W',(0xfd,0xfd,0xfb)),  # white eyes
]
def classify(r,g,b):
    best=None;bd=1e9
    for ch,(tr,tg,tb) in PAL:
        d=abs(r-tr)+abs(g-tg)+abs(b-tb)
        if d<bd: bd=d;best=ch
    return best if bd<90 else ('.' if r+g+b>330 else ' ')

w,h,nch,buf = read_png(sys.argv[1])
cols=120; rows=90
cw=w/cols; ch=h/rows
out=[]
for ry in range(rows):
    line=[]
    for rx in range(cols):
        x0=int(rx*cw); y0=int(ry*ch)
        votes={}
        for yy in range(y0,max(y0+1,int((ry+1)*ch)),max(1,int(ch//3))):
            for xx in range(x0,max(x0+1,int((rx+1)*cw)),max(1,int(cw//3))):
                i=(yy*w+xx)*nch
                c=classify(buf[i],buf[i+1],buf[i+2])
                votes[c]=votes.get(c,0)+1
        line.append(max(votes,key=votes.get))
    out.append(''.join(line))
print('\n'.join(out))
EOF

All four deliverables verify. Final cleanup done. Here's a summary of what I made:

## Awkward Robot Family Portrait

**Deliverables in `./output/`** (4 files, all well under 2MB):
- **`awkward-robot-family-portrait.svg`** — the artwork (1200×1200 vector)
- **`awkward-robot-family-portrait-animated.svg`** — SMIL-animated variant (wagging tail, head tilt, spinning propeller, dad's nervous hover-hand bob, son's stiff wave, mom's sweat-drop pulse; degrades gracefully to the static pose in non-animating viewers)
- **`awkward-robot-family-portrait.png`** — 1800×1800 lossless render (1.4MB)
- **`awkward-robot-family-portrait.jpg`** — 1800×1800 compressed render (177KB)

**The scene** — a classic studio setup: mottled warm-gray backdrop, soft key-light halo, floor seam, potted plants, contact shadows, vignette. Seven robots, each with a distinct personality, relationships told entirely through pose:

- **Grandpa** (rust, hunched, flat cap, monocle, brush mustache, bent antenna) — not looking at the camera; he gazes down at a tiny locket photo of grandma he's raised in his hand, leaning on his cane
- **Mom** (cream & rose, pearls, purse) — tight strained smile with a pulsing sweat drop; her hand rests protectively on her daughter's shoulder
- **Dad** (big steel-blue, crooked striped tie, pocket protector) — cheesy wink, huge grin, enthusiastic thumbs-up… and the classic **hovering hand** stretched across a conspicuous gap over the teen's shoulder, never quite committing to touching
- **Teen** (graphite + neon, headphones, light-up sneakers) — arms crossed, leaning away, eyes rolled sideways, refusing the red "family accent" everyone else wears
- **Daughter** (teal, cable pigtail curls with red bow) — criss-cross seated, shyly hugging her plush cat
- **Little son** (yellow, propeller beanie) — propped on hands, enormous unblinking pupils, wide frozen grin, one arm raised in a reluctant wave
- **Robot dog** (silver tin, asymmetric ears, tongue out) — head tilted, tail wagging, staring up at his boy

No text anywhere. Source lives in the workdir root (`family.svg`, `family_animated.svg`) with the render/verify toolchain in `src/` — including a pure-Python PNG inspector I used to visually verify every render, since no SVG rasterizer was available (rendered via macOS QuickLook, which required a square canvas to avoid a scaling/cropping quirk I diagnosed empirically).
